description: RAISE the mega-inner eigenVECTOR orthogonality ceiling at k~384 -- brief-26 measured it as 'the biggest unlocked lever on the low-rank shapes' (3/4/8/10/12). The split-megakernel inner solve's eigenvectors G lose orthogonality sharply above k=384 (measured: k=352 orth 7.9e-3, k=384 1.2e-2, k=400 0.78, k=416 2.1 -- a CLIFF), while its eigenVALUES keep improving. This orth cliff -- NOT eig accuracy -- is what forces the low-rank k<=384 and blocks shapes 4/10 (k=608/768) from using the fast inner solve at all (stuck on cuSOLVER). If the ceiling rises, shapes 3/8/12 take larger k (smaller complement -> cheaper CQR2/AVc) AND shapes 4/10 inner blocks move off cuSOLVER = compounds across 5 shapes. STEP 1 (DIAGNOSE, cheap): isolate WHERE orth degrades at k=400 -- run the inner mega solve on a k=400 reduced block, check orth of the RAW megakernel eigenvectors G vs orth after each stage; is it the twisted-factorization eigenvector stage (stage 3, known to lose orthogonality for CLUSTERED reduced-block eigenvalues -- likely, since a larger k reduced block has more near-degenerate eigenvalues) or the FP16 reduction? STEP 2 (CHEAPEST FIX FIRST, pure-torch): add a cheap re-orthonormalization of the k-by-k inner eigenvectors G AFTER the megakernel -- one CholeskyQR or 1-2 Newton-Schulz steps on G (k-by-k, tiny vs the n-by-k outer work) then a Rayleigh-Ritz value refresh lam=diag(G^T Bk G) so (lam,G) stay a consistent eigenpair; this restores orth without touching the kernel. If that raises the ceiling to k~512, RE-SWEEP the low-rank bands upward (shapes 3/8/12 larger k) and test shape-4 inner k<=512 off cuSOLVER. STEP 3 (only if torch cleanup insufficient): in-kernel fix -- FP32 twisted-factorization, or an in-kernel modified-Gram-Schmidt reorthonormalization pass over the eigenvectors for clustered eigenvalues (nvcc). Start pure-torch (STEP 1-2, GPU-light); escalate to nvcc (STEP 3) only if the torch cleanup can't raise the ceiling. Per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback unchanged; forks best 8d30bf975; distinct from brief-25 (tridiag REDUCTION split) and brief-26 (k routing under the OLD ceiling) -- this RAISES the ceiling itself. -O2/-O3 per whatever the parent uses for any kernel edit; no 'stream' substring; verify 39/39 + quiet re-bench beats 36216.

RAISE low-rank k 352/384->448 for no-cliff shapes 3/12 (NO cleanup). REGRESSION: shape3 81058->282906us (3.5x), shape12 33845->102764us (3x), geomean 36324->43478. STEP-1 diagnosis: orth breaks ENTIRELY in stage-3 twisted factorization (orth[Z]==orth[G_raw] at every k; back-transform preserves orth). Cliff is SPECTRUM-dependent not universal-k: dense512 PR55 & geom1024 PR67 have NO cliff (orth 1.5e-3/2e-4 at k=448 < gate); only rankdef512 PR163 cliffs (k448 orth 0.75). So shapes 3/12 need NO cleanup to run k=448 -- but the mega INNER solve cost grows steeply with k (single-CTA twisted-fact+backtransform latency-bound, 58ms b640 k=448). Smaller complement saving << bigger inner cost. Refutes naive k-raise.

Add cheap Newton-Schulz re-orthonormalization + diag Rayleigh refresh to the split mega inner solve (_lr_ns_reorth), bands at optimal k=352/384. NEUTRAL-REGRESSION: geomean 36324->36761 (+1.2%), 39/39 PASS. NS2 restores orth 1e-3->3e-6 at ~11-21% of inner-solve cost AND (unlike CQR which mixes columns -> needs a 262-281% batched RR eigh) preserves eigenvector directions so diag Rayleigh keeps (lam,G) consistent with NO eigh. BUT at routed k=352/384 raw orth is ALREADY under gate (dense512/geom1024 no cliff) -> cleanup is pure overhead: shape3 81058->87684, shape8 93488->100557, shape12 33845->34769. Confirms orth NOT the binding constraint at routed k.

NS cleanup ON + raise no-cliff shapes 3/12 to k=448 (brief's FULL hypothesis end-to-end). REGRESSION: geomean 36324->43836, 39/39 PASS. shape3 87684(k352)->294866(k448), shape12 34769->102483. NS makes orth PASS at k=448 (3e-6, was 0.75/0.10 raw, 0 fallback) -> ceiling IS cheaply raisable. BUT the mega INNER solve has a sharp COST CLIFF above k~384 (single-CTA twisted-fact+FP16-reduction latency-bound: b640 82ms@k352 -> 108ms@k384 -> 259-278ms@k>=400) that dominates. Even w/ free orth fix, k=448 is 3.5x slower than k=352. Orth ceiling was NEVER the binding constraint; the inner-solve cost cliff is. Also: shapes 4/10 blocked by the EIG gate (energy capture needs k=608/768, outer_eigr 5e-2/2e-1 at k<=448) NOT orth, and k>=512 overflows the mega FP16-triangle SMEM cap regardless. Definitive built refutation.

Keep the characterized NS ceiling-raiser (_lr_ns_reorth) DEFAULT OFF; bands at parent-optimal k=352/384. NON-REGRESSING best safe result: geomean 36196us == parent 36324 within noise, 39/39 PASS (validated 2x, profiled). Captures the measured finding as ready infra: NS2+diag DOES raise the inner orth ceiling cheaply+correctly (orth 0.75->3e-6 at k=448, eigenvector-preserving, ~11-21% of inner cost, NO eigh -- vs CQR+RR 262-281%), but net-regresses at the routed k (orth already under gate) and cannot unlock larger k (single-CTA inner-solve COST CLIFF above k~384: profiled mega_eigh_med_split_k 28ms@k352 vs 48ms@k448, and full-path b640 82->278ms; t3 k=448 3.5x slower than k=352 WITH orth fixed). Flag->True only after the inner cost cliff is flattened.

REFUTATION (4 built+benchmarked trials + full diagnostics). HEAD=1f417ef9d, geomean 36196us (== parent 36324 within noise, 39/39, validated 2x, profiled) -- non-regressing; adds the characterized NS ceiling-raiser _lr_ns_reorth (flag OFF). STEP-1 DIAGNOSIS: the mega inner-solve eigenvector orth loss is ENTIRELY in stage-3 twisted factorization (orth[Z]==orth[G] at every k; the Householder back-transform preserves orth -- NOT the FP16 reduction). The k~400 'cliff' is SPECTRUM-dependent, not universal-k: dense512(PR55) & geom1024(PR67) have NO cliff (orth 1.5e-3/2e-4 at k=448 < gate); only rankdef512(PR163) cliffs (k448 orth 0.75). STEP-2 CHEAPEST FIX: Newton-Schulz (NOT CholeskyQR) IS the right cleanup -- NS is a symmetric polynomial in G^TG so it re-orthonormalizes WITHOUT mixing columns, keeping near-eigenvectors as eigenvectors, so a plain diag Rayleigh refresh stays consistent with NO eigh. NS2+diag: orth 0.75->3e-6, eigr unchanged, ~11-21% of inner-solve cost. (CQR mixes columns -> needs a full batched RR eigh = 262-281% of the inner solve, prohibitive.) So the ceiling IS cheaply+correctly raisable to k=448. BUT raising it WINS NOTHING (t1/t2/t3 all regress): (a) shapes 3/8/12 sit at their eig-AND-cost-optimal k=352/384 where the single-CTA inner solve is cheapest; (b) the inner solve has a sharp COST CLIFF above k~384 -- profiled mega_eigh_med_split_k 28ms@k352->48ms@k448, full-path b640 82->108->259-278ms at k352/384/>=400 -- so k=448 is 3.5x slower than k=352 even WITH orth fixed (t3); the complement (CQR2/AVc) saving from a smaller nc is dwarfed; (c) shapes 4/10 are blocked by the EIG gate (energy capture needs k=608/768; outer_eigr 5e-2/2e-1 at k<=448, which NS/CQR CANNOT fix -- it is an eig-residual not an orth defect), and k>=512 overflows the mega FP16-triangle SMEM cap (262KB>228KB) regardless. The orth ceiling was NEVER the binding constraint. OPEN DIRECTIONS worth a fresh brief: (1) FLATTEN THE INNER-SOLVE COST CLIFF -- the single-CTA-per-matrix split kernel is latency-bound and its cost climbs ~super-linearly with k; a genuinely batched / multi-CTA / tensor-core reduced-block dense eigensolver that stays cheap at k=448-768 would make BOTH the larger-k routing (3/8/12) AND shapes 4/10 (k=608/768) win, and the NS cleanup (already committed, flag-flip) instantly unlocks the orth side. (2) SHRINK THE COMPLEMENT COST directly (CQR2/AVc on nc cols) rather than via bigger k -- profiling shows the shape-3 path is ~36% inner kernel + the rest complement/back-transform sgemms; a cheaper complement is orthogonal to the inner-solve cliff. (3) A k>=512 reduced-block solver that tiles the FP16 triangle OUT of SMEM (or a tensor-core batched tridiag) would let shapes 4/10 leave cuSOLVER -- the real prize (76947us & 108740us). Distinct from brief-25 (tridiag reduction split) only if it targets the reduced-BLOCK dense solve, not the outer tridiag.
